UnitStatement: nonlinear_supports crate classifies nonlinear support states for iterative mechanics solves; it does not assemble a global solve, encode design-code checks, provide support catalog defaults, or make professional approval claims.
ActivationSense enum encodes a nonlinear support's reaction sign convention: PositiveReaction or NegativeReaction.
GapDirection enum encodes the displacement sense in which a gap closes: PositiveDisplacement or NegativeDisplacement.
NonlinearSupportBehavior enum has four variants: OneWay (active_when), Gap (closes_when), LiftOff (contact_when), and Friction.
NonlinearSupport struct holds support_id, node_index, dof (FrameDof), behavior, optional gap clearance, and optional friction_coefficient.
NonlinearSupportUnitMetadata struct holds a unit_system_ref plus displacement, reaction, and friction_coefficient quantity-unit metadata.
NonlinearSupportUnitMetadata.has_expected_dimensions requires displacement=Displacement, reaction=Force, and friction coefficient=Dimensionless canonical dimensions.
NonlinearSupport::one_way constructs a one-way support with an explicit activation reaction sense and no gap or friction coefficient.
NonlinearSupport::gap constructs a gap support; it validates the clearance is nonnegative and finite before recording it.
NonlinearSupport::lift_off constructs a lift-off support with an explicit contact reaction sense.
NonlinearSupport::friction constructs a friction support after validating the friction coefficient is nonnegative and finite.
ActiveSetState enum has four states: Active, Inactive, Sticking, Sliding.
TrialSupportState holds support_id, displacement, reaction, and optional normal_reaction and tangential_reaction; constructor validates displacement and reaction are finite.
TrialSupportState.with_friction_reactions records validated finite normal and tangential reactions for friction classification.
ActiveSetIterationInput carries iteration, max_iterations, tolerance, supports, trial_states, and prior_states for one active-set evaluation.
ActiveSetIteration holds iteration, support states, changed_supports, residual_norm, converged flag, and diagnostics.
ActiveSetIteration.is_blocked returns true when any diagnostic has Blocking or Failure severity.
ActiveSetIteration.to_report_record validates tolerance is nonnegative finite and builds an ActiveSetReportRecord with assumptions and limitations.
ActiveSetReportRecord captures iteration, max_iterations, tolerance, residual_norm, converged, per-support report states, changed_supports, diagnostics, assumptions, and limitations.
Active-set report assumption: trial displacement and reaction facts are supplied by an external mechanics solve.
Active-set report assumption: the active-set residual norm is the count of support states changed in the bounded iteration record.
Active-set report limitation: this crate does not assemble or solve the global nonlinear system.
Active-set report limitation: production tolerance policy, sparse solver selection, final constraint strategy, and result-envelope integration remain outside this bounded crate.
Active-set report limitation: the record is mechanics-reporting evidence only and does not state rule compliance or professional approval.
NonlinearSupportError enum variants: NonFiniteInput, NegativeInput, MissingGap, MissingFrictionCoefficient, MissingTrialState, MissingFrictionData.

diagnostic_from_nonlinear_support_error maps missing-gap, missing-friction-coefficient, missing-trial-state, and missing-friction-data errors to Blocking InvalidRestraint solver diagnostics with remediation.
diagnostic_from_nonlinear_support_error maps non-finite and negative numeric input errors to a Blocking InvalidNumericInput diagnostic.

evaluate_active_set_iteration validates tolerance, finds each support's trial state, classifies state, tracks changed supports, sorts deterministically, and computes residual_norm as the changed-support count.
evaluate_active_set_iteration errors with MissingTrialState when a support has no matching trial state.
An active-set iteration is converged when residual_norm (changed-support count) is less than or equal to the tolerance.
evaluate_active_set_report runs evaluate_active_set_iteration and converts the result to a report record.
classify_support_state dispatches on support behavior to return an ActiveSetState from the trial state.
OneWay support state is derived from the trial reaction sign via state_from_sense with the support's active_when sense.
Gap support requires an explicit gap clearance (else MissingGap); it is Active when the trial displacement reaches the clearance in the closing direction, else Inactive.
Friction support classification requires normal and tangential reaction data (else MissingFrictionData); nonpositive normal reaction yields Inactive.
Friction support is Sticking when |tangential| <= coefficient*|normal| and Sliding otherwise; the coefficient must be present, nonnegative, and finite.
with_active_set_context augments a NonConvergence diagnostic message with the changed supports and per-support state summary and sets affected_ref to active-set:<changed>.
nonconvergence_code returns the NonConvergence diagnostic code from an active-set iteration when present.
state_from_sense returns Active when the trial reaction matches the activation sense (positive>0 or negative<0), else Inactive.
validate_finite rejects non-finite f64 inputs with NonFiniteInput.
validate_nonnegative_finite rejects non-finite inputs and negative values with NegativeInput.

nonlinear_supports unit tests cover one-way activation, gap closure with/without clearance, lift-off deactivation, friction sticking/sliding/inactive cases, missing-coefficient and non-finite rejection, unit-metadata dimensions, and active-set convergence/nonconvergence reporting.
performance_harness crate (open_pipe_stress_solver_performance_harness) depends on frame_kernel, solver diagnostics, and sparse_direct; not published.

The Solver Performance Harness is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-04-05, providing a deterministic regression harness around the frame-kernel solve boundary to record performance and conditioning evidence without changing solver logic.
Since human ruling DEC-023 the harness measures the in-repo sparse skyline path (core/solver/sparse_direct) alongside the dense path on the same reduced systems.
Harness scope includes invented frame-chain and planar grid-frame benchmark fixtures with explicit public provenance posture.
Harness records repeat-run regression records for the same fixture, solver version, and harness settings, including per-repeat residual and solution-delta observations.
Harness records matrix size, nonzero-count, residual, repeatability, diagonal conditioning observations, and condition-ratio estimates for the dense path.

SparseSolveObservation records RCM ordering identity, original/ordered profile entry counts and half-bandwidths, accepted-pivot extrema, the pivot-ratio conditioning proxy, nonpositive-pivot count, sparse-vs-dense parity delta, sparse residual, repeat determinism delta, and elapsed time.
Elapsed-time measurements are environment-dependent observations recorded for measurement only; no timing thresholds are asserted (thresholds remain governed by D-04).

Harness integrates solver diagnostics in a fixed order: DEC-023 sparse-adoption diagnostic, tolerance-policy TBD diagnostic, dense conditioning classification, dense solve failures, sparse factorization-report diagnostics, sparse conditioning classification, and sparse solve failures.

Harness boundary: it does not set release-quality timing thresholds, alter the frame kernel or sparse solver, define code-specific checks, encode protected standards examples, or make professional/code-compliance claims.

The live product solve path still uses the dense verification interface from frame_kernel; per DEC-023 the dense path also serves as the parity oracle for the in-repo sparse skyline path, whose live adoption remains TBD and is recorded as such in every run record.

Fixture unit metadata declares the calculation basis for reproducibility only; the harness does not define a conversion catalog, convert units, supply protected benchmark values, or promote fixture results to release-quality evidence.

Sparse-vs-dense parity assertions cite the DEC-026 analytic-class relative seed (1.0e-9) scaled by the dense reference solution magnitude; the harness records parity deltas without asserting thresholds.
SPARSE_ORDERING_ALGORITHM_ID constant identifies the deterministic sparse ordering algorithm as reverse-cuthill-mckee-deterministic.
FixtureProvenanceStatus enum: InventedPublic, PublicPermissive, UnknownSource, ProtectedSuspected.
FixtureProvenance records source_name, source_location, redistribution_status, and a review_note.
BenchmarkFixture holds fixture_id, name, provenance, unit_basis, node_count, elements, force vector, and restrained_dofs.
HarnessSettings holds solver_version, repeat_count, and optional condition warning/failure thresholds.
RepeatRunObservation records repeat_index, max-abs solution delta from the first solve, and max-abs residual.
ConditioningObservation records matrix dimension, finite and zero diagonal counts, min/max abs diagonal, and a diagonal condition-ratio estimate.
SparseSolveObservation records all sparse-path measurements alongside the dense path; all fields are measurements with no asserted thresholds (governed by D-04).

HarnessRunRecord aggregates per-fixture matrix counts, repeat observations, conditioning observation, condition-ratio estimate, dense and sparse timing/observations, diagnostics, assumptions, limitations, and provenance notes.
HarnessSuiteRunRecord holds suite_id, suite_name, solver_version, fixture element counts, fixture records, summary, assumptions, limitations, and provenance notes.
HarnessSuiteSummary aggregates fixture, node, element, DOF, nonzero, repeat-observation, diagnostic, and sparse-observation counts plus max solution-delta and residual values across the suite.
HarnessError enum: InvalidSetting, InvalidFixtureProvenance, FrameKernel, Diagnostics, SparseDirect.
HarnessSettings default uses solver_version TBD, repeat_count 2, and no condition thresholds.
DEFAULT_INVENTED_SUITE_ELEMENT_COUNTS is [1, 2, 4, 8].

invented_cantilever_chain_fixture builds an invented cantilever chain of the given element count (must be >=1) with a synthetic section, contiguous nodes, a tip load, and a fully restrained first node.

invented_grid_frame_fixture builds a synthetic planar grid frame (x_count,y_count each >=2): row-major nodes, horizontal/vertical frame elements, fully restrained bottom row, and an invented lateral load at the last top-row node.
run_default_invented_fixture_suite runs the invented fixture suite over DEFAULT_INVENTED_SUITE_ELEMENT_COUNTS.
run_invented_fixture_suite validates fixture sizes and settings, runs each cantilever-chain fixture, and assembles a suite record.
run_fixture_repeat runs both the dense path and the DEC-023 sparse skyline path on the same reduced system with a fixed deterministic diagnostic ordering.
run_fixture_repeat measures the first dense solve; on dense failure it records a frame-error diagnostic and still observes the sparse path.
run_fixture_repeat performs repeat dense solves, recording per-repeat solution deltas from the first solve and residuals.
observe_sparse_path measures the DEC-023 sparse skyline path on the reduced system, returning an observation when it completes plus sparse diagnostics in deterministic order.
observe_sparse_path performs repeat sparse solves to record the max-abs repeat solution delta (determinism check).
suite_record builds a HarnessSuiteRunRecord with a suite summary, size-labeled suite_id, aggregated provenance notes, and fixed suite assumptions/limitations.
Suite assumption: the suite uses only invented cantilever-chain fixtures; single-fixture records remain the authority for per-fixture matrix and diagnostic observations.
Suite limitation: fixture sizes are explicit invented coverage points (not approved practical-size bands), live sparse adoption remains TBD, and release thresholds remain TBD.
suite_summary aggregates counts and extrema across fixture records, including sparse-observation profile counts and parity/residual maxima.
run_record assembles a HarnessRunRecord from fixture, settings, matrices, observations, and diagnostics with fixed assumptions and limitations.
Run-record assumption: the frame-kernel dense solve path serves as the parity oracle for the DEC-023 sparse skyline path, observed with the in-repo skyline LDLT solver.

Run-record limitation: live sparse adoption remains TBD; release timing/memory/conditioning thresholds remain TBD; elapsed-time observations are measurements, not asserted thresholds; hardware-normalized gates are not claimed.

validate_fixture rejects fixtures whose provenance is not InventedPublic or PublicPermissive, whose force length mismatches node_count*DOF_PER_NODE, or whose unit basis lacks the frame-kernel canonical dimensions.
validate_suite_fixture_sizes rejects an empty fixture-element-count list.
invented_frame_unit_basis declares invented unit identifiers for length, force, moment, stress, area, second-moment-area, displacement, and rotation.
validate_settings rejects a zero repeat_count and requires condition warning and failure thresholds to be supplied together (both or neither).
observe_diagonal_conditioning computes finite/zero diagonal counts, min/max abs diagonal, and the diagonal condition-ratio estimate (max/min) when min is finite and positive.
nonzero_count counts matrix entries whose absolute value exceeds zero.
max_abs_delta returns the max absolute element-wise difference between two vectors.
max_abs_residual returns the max absolute entry of (A*x - b).

performance_harness unit tests cover deterministic repeat records, suite summary counts, default suite sizes, empty/zero-element rejection, conditioning observation and thresholds, singular-repeat and located sparse-singular diagnostics, sparse-vs-dense parity on chain and grid fixtures, suite sparse aggregation, and provenance/setting rejection.
sparse_direct crate (open_pipe_stress_sparse_direct) is a code-neutral in-repo sparse skyline direct solver with no runtime dependencies; frame_kernel is a dev-dependency only.

The Sparse Skyline Direct Solver is the first bounded implementation slice of human ruling DEC-023 (decision D-03 Option C); it provides bandwidth/profile-reducing DOF ordering, skyline storage of the symmetric stiffness matrix, and an in-repo LDL^T profile factorization and solve, supporting DEL-04-01 within PKG-04.
Sparse-direct scope: deterministic reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering over a node adjacency structure or dense-matrix nonzero pattern.
Sparse-direct scope: skyline (profile/envelope) storage of a symmetric matrix as the lower triangle by rows, each row spanning its first nonzero column to the diagonal.
Sparse-direct scope: in-repo LDL^T profile factorization with a fixed operation order and no pivot reordering.
Sparse-direct scope: a solve_symmetric_system seam that orders, stores, factors, and solves a dense symmetric system and returns ordering, profile, and factorization observations (FR-008).

Sparse-direct scope: factorization reporting of singular pivot location (ordered and original indices), accepted-pivot extrema, a pivot-ratio conditioning proxy, and nonpositive-pivot count and first location.

The sparse ordering is reverse Cuthill-McKee, chosen as the classic bandwidth/profile-reducing ordering for banded/branched frame topologies and as a pure breadth-first traversal admitting a fully deterministic formulation.
RCM determinism: the result is a pure function of the undirected graph; adjacency lists are symmetrized, sorted, and deduplicated so caller list order cannot change the result.
RCM determinism: connected components are processed in order of their lowest original node index.
RCM determinism: each component starts from a pseudo-peripheral node found by level-structure iteration, with every tie broken by ascending (degree, original index).

RCM determinism: breadth-first neighbor visits are ordered by ascending (degree, original index), and the concatenated order is reversed once at the end; no randomization, threading, or platform-dependent iteration order is used.

The factorization and solve are single-threaded straight-line f64 arithmetic with a fixed operation order, no reassociation/blocking/SIMD/parallel reduction, preserving byte-reproducibility like the dense path; repeat-run bitwise identity is asserted in tests.

SPARSE_SOLVE_ZERO_PIVOT_GUARD = 1.0e-12 mirrors the dense DENSE_SOLVE_ZERO_PIVOT_GUARD precedent; it is an internal verification guard, not the project solver tolerance policy (governed under D-04, DEC-026).
A pivot at or below the guard fails as SingularPivot reporting both the profile-ordered index and the original pre-ordering index so the failure traces to a reduced DOF.
Accepted negative pivots are never silently absorbed: the report carries nonpositive_pivot_count and first location; nonpositive pivots indicate the reduced system is not positive definite.
pivot_condition_ratio_estimate is max|d|/min|d| over accepted LDL^T pivots, a documented conditioning proxy not a true condition number; no thresholds are encoded (governed by D-04).

Symmetric-input contract: the solver reads only one triangle; for any index pair it reads the original lower-triangle entry dense[max][min]. Input symmetry is the caller's contract, keeping construction deterministic under last-ulp asymmetry.
Sparse-direct has zero external dependencies (Rust standard library only), matching sibling solver crates and the DEC-023 requirement; the frame kernel is only a dev-dependency for parity tests.

Sparse-direct computes open numerical-mechanics quantities only; it does not encode compliance rules, code-specific values, protected standards content, material allowables, private project data, or approval claims; all test models are invented.

Sparse-direct unit tests cover deterministic RCM ordering, profile round-trips, exact hand-checked LDL^T factorization and solve, singular-pivot location in both numberings, nonpositive-pivot counting, invalid-input handling, repeat-run bitwise determinism, and sparse-vs-dense parity citing the DEC-026 1.0e-9 seed.
Integration status: the live product solve path still uses the dense verification interface; binding it to this sparse solver is a separate bounded tranche recorded by the SparseSolverTbd diagnostic.

sparse_direct crate implements DEC-023 (D-03 Option C): deterministic RCM DOF ordering, skyline storage of the symmetric stiffness matrix, and an in-repo LDL^T profile factorization and solve, with no design-code, protected-standards, or private-data content.
SPARSE_SOLVE_ZERO_PIVOT_GUARD public constant is 1.0e-12.
SparseDirectError enum: InvalidMatrixDimensions, InvalidVectorLength, NonFiniteInput, InvalidOrdering, and SingularPivot (with ordered and original indices).
SparseDirectError::SingularPivot reports the pivot position in the profile-ordered numbering and the corresponding original input-matrix row index.
PivotLocation records a pivot location in both the profile-ordered numbering and the caller's original pre-ordering numbering.
FactorizationReport records dimension, profile entry count, max half-bandwidth, min/max abs pivot, pivot-condition-ratio estimate, nonpositive pivot count, and first nonpositive pivot location.
SymmetricProfileMatrix stores a symmetric matrix in skyline (profile) form: lower triangle by rows, reading entry dense[max][min] for each index pair to stay deterministic under last-ulp asymmetry.
SymmetricProfileMatrix::from_dense builds profile storage from a dense symmetric matrix in identity ordering.
SymmetricProfileMatrix::from_dense_with_order builds profile storage under a given ordering permutation where order[k] is the original index of the k-th ordered row/column.
SymmetricProfileMatrix.profile_entry_count returns the number of stored skyline entries including diagonals.
SymmetricProfileMatrix.max_half_bandwidth returns the maximum row half-bandwidth i - first_columns[i] over all rows.
SymmetricProfileMatrix.get returns the entry at ordered position (row,col), zero outside the stored profile.
ProfileFactorization holds the LDL^T factor (strictly-lower profile entries hold L with implied unit diagonal; diagonal holds D) and its FactorizationReport.

ProfileFactorization.solve_ordered solves A x = rhs in the ordered numbering with a fixed operation order: forward substitution (ascending rows/cols), diagonal scaling, then backward substitution (descending rows, ascending cols).

factorize_ldlt performs LDL^T profile factorization with a fixed deterministic operation order and no pivot reordering; pivots at or below the guard fail as SingularPivot and accepted negative pivots are counted and located.
factorize_ldlt rejects a non-finite computed pivot with NonFiniteInput.

adjacency_from_dense builds undirected node adjacency from a dense symmetric matrix's exact nonzero pattern; an edge exists when either mirrored entry is nonzero, and exact zero tests keep the pattern deterministic.

reverse_cuthill_mckee returns a deterministic RCM permutation (order[k]=original index of k-th ordered node): symmetrized/sorted/deduped adjacency, components by lowest original index, pseudo-peripheral start nodes, and ties broken by ascending (degree, original index).
reverse_cuthill_mckee rejects an adjacency index outside the node count with InvalidOrdering.
pseudo_peripheral_start finds a component's start node by iterating level structures, choosing the candidate with greatest eccentricity, ties broken by min (degree, index).
bfs_reachable returns all nodes reachable from a seed via breadth-first traversal.
bfs_eccentricity returns the eccentricity (level count) from a start node and the nodes in its last BFS level.
min_by_degree_then_index returns the node minimizing (degree, index) among the given nodes.
SparseSolveResult records the solution in caller numbering, the RCM ordering, original/ordered max half-bandwidths and profile entry counts, and the factorization report (FR-008, DEC-023).

solve_symmetric_system orders (RCM), stores (profile), factors (LDL^T), and solves a dense symmetric system, then inverse-permutes the solution back to the caller's numbering, returning ordering and factorization observations.
solve_symmetric_system validates the matrix is square, the force length matches the dimension, and all entries are finite before solving.
symmetric_entry reads the lower-triangle entry dense[max][min] for an index pair.
validate_square verifies the matrix is square and all rows are finite, returning the dimension.
validate_finite_slice rejects any non-finite value in a slice with NonFiniteInput.
validate_permutation verifies an ordering has the right length, indices within range, and no repeats, else InvalidOrdering.

sparse_direct unit tests cover RCM ordering on path/star/disconnected/scrambled graphs with tie-breaks and symmetrization, profile round-trips, exact LDL^T factorization and solve, singular- and nonpositive-pivot reporting in both numberings, invalid-input rejection, bitwise repeat determinism, and sparse-vs-dense parity citing the DEC-026 1.0e-9 seed.
DEC026_ANALYTIC_RELATIVE_SEED test constant is 1.0e-9, the DEC-026 analytic reference-result relative seed scaled by the dense solution magnitude rather than inventing a new tolerance.
straight_pipe crate (open_pipe_stress_straight_pipe) provides straight pipe element mechanics and depends on frame_kernel; not published.

The Straight Pipe Element crate is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-04-02; it adapts explicit straight-pipe section and mass properties into the existing 3D frame kernel, exposes weight hooks for later load-case work, and recovers local mechanical element forces.
Straight-pipe scope: straight two-node pipe element construction.
Straight-pipe scope: explicit section-property integration through caller-supplied area, second moments, and torsion constant.
Straight-pipe scope: explicit mass-per-length and weight-per-length hooks.
Straight-pipe scope: local element displacement and force recovery using the frame-kernel stiffness and orientation conventions.
Straight-pipe scope: direct local end-resultant recovery for pipe end I or J using the solver force-vector components without sign reinterpretation or stress-rule classification.

Straight-pipe boundary: it does not provide pipe dimension tables, material defaults, code-specific values, stress checks, load combinations, or compliance claims; inputs are mechanics quantities governed by upstream schemas, unit contracts, provenance checks, and section-property calculations.

StraightPipeBoundaryMetadata is the external solver-facing boundary: it binds the straight-pipe numeric fields to a caller-supplied frame-kernel unit basis, mass-per-length, gravity, and force_per_length unit metadata plus canonical model references, recording identifiers only without unit conversion or engineering defaults.

Straight-pipe unit tests cover section-property validation, frame-kernel stiffness integration, weight hooks, axial local force recovery, direct end-resultant recovery, transverse bending recovery, and displacement-length validation.
